amlodipine5.primaryEffect: Relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure and reduce cardiac workload.
amlodipine5.sideEffects: Ankle swelling, dizziness, flushing, and palpitations.

norvasc5.primaryEffect: Blocks calcium entry into vascular muscle, allowing vessels to widen.
norvasc5.sideEffects: Peripheral edema, fatigue, nausea, and abdominal pain.

amlodipine10.primaryEffect: Provides long-acting blood pressure control and improves cardiac oxygen supply.
amlodipine10.sideEffects: Edema, headache, drowsiness, and rapid heartbeat.

emergency.title: Emergency info
emergency.medicationWarning: Call 119 immediately for trouble breathing or swelling of the face or throat.
emergency.chooseFirstAid: Choose the first-aid information you need

woundSteps.step1: Make sure the area is safe and wash your hands; avoid direct contact with blood.
woundSteps.step2: Apply continuous direct pressure with clean gauze to stop bleeding.
woundSteps.step3: After bleeding stops, rinse with saline or clean drinking water.
woundSteps.step4: Cover with a clean dressing, then wrap and secure it.

emergency.woundWarning: Call 119 for heavy bleeding, an embedded object, or bleeding that will not stop. Do not remove an embedded object.

pregnancySteps.step1: Stop activity. Sit safely or lie on the left side and keep breathing freely.
pregnancySteps.step2: Have someone stay with you, prepare your maternity record, and contact your maternity provider.
pregnancySteps.step3: Do not take medicine on your own; follow instructions from 119 or medical staff.

emergency.pregnancyWarning: Call 119 now for heavy bleeding, broken waters, persistent or severe abdominal pain, trouble breathing, fainting, or seizures.
emergency.cprWarning: Adult quick guide only. Keep following instructions from 119 and the AED.

cprSteps.step1Body: Make sure the scene is safe. Tap both shoulders and shout. If there is no response, continue.
cprSteps.step2Body: Shout for help. Tell a specific person to call 119 and bring an AED. Use speakerphone and do not hang up.
cprSteps.step3Body: Watch for normal chest and abdominal movement. If there is no breathing or only gasping, start compressions now.
cprSteps.step4Body: Stack the heels of your hands in the center of the chest and lock your elbows. For an adult, press 5–6 cm, allow full recoil, and minimize pauses.
cprSteps.step5Body: Turn on the AED, expose the chest, and attach the pads. Make sure no one touches the person during analysis or shock.
cprSteps.step6Body: Follow the AED and resume compressions. Continue until normal breathing returns, rescuers take over, or you cannot continue.
